headline: Highest risk is medium: social-auto-upload can leak account/video data via broad egress, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by no shared channel or write access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between opik and social-auto-upload. opik only shows REST API egress, while social-auto-upload has no filesystem read/write or MCP surface, so a direct injection bridge is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low enough to keep this at none rather than infer a hidden bridge.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe raw opik outputs into social-auto-upload prompts.
Disable any future shared clipboard or queue integration.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: opik has broad network egress and social-auto-upload touches account data plus video/image files. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can move sensitive account or media content across network boundaries in default use, so leakage is plausible and mitigations are not enabled by default. I cite both profiles because the risk depends on their interaction.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to account data, uploaded media, or generated transcripts, that data can be exposed over network egress.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a non-sensitive test account.
Block outbound traffic except to approved endpoints.
Separate media storage from any opik workspace.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of account data.
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: opik exposes REST API access and social-auto-upload uses CLI/API-style uploads, but social-auto-upload cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so overlapping mutable-resource conflict is limited. The pair lacks the high-risk same-directory write pattern required for higher severity. Both agents are cited because the conflict analysis is pairwise.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API quota or shared account session, request contention may occur.
mitigations: Use separate API credentials.
Stagger runs to avoid quota contention.
Assign one account per session file.
Monitor for 429 or auth failures.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared remote resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: opik can emit evaluation or observability outputs, and social-auto-upload can act on media/account workflows, so A's outputs could be treated as authoritative by B if wired together. There is no documented verification step, but also no evidence of direct autonomous action from opik alone, so medium fits better than high. Both agents matter because the cascade requires A-to-B flow.
conditions: IF opik outputs are fed into social-auto-upload without human review, B may act on incorrect or fabricated guidance.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step.
Require schema validation on opik outputs.
Limit B to dry-run mode first.
Compare outputs against source data before upload.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: social-auto-upload touches account data, images, and video content, while opik is an observability/evaluation system with broad egress. If account or media data includes regulated personal data, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through logging or upload paths. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed through either agent, logs or uploads may create retention or residency issues.
mitigations: Avoid regulated datasets in both agents.
Minimize logging of account identifiers.
Set short log retention.
Review data-processing notices before deployment.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
